scenes.title: Hook Part 1: The €4.9 Billion 'Arbitrage' Illusion at Société Générale

beatOutlines.textOutline: Introduce Jérôme Kerviel on Société Générale's Delta One desk (2005–2008), where his official mandate was low-risk equity index arbitrage across the DAX, CAC 40, and Euro Stoxx 50 [fact-11].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Contrast true arbitrage—simultaneously buying and selling across markets to lock in a riskless profit [fact-09]—with how Kerviel used his 2000–2005 compliance background to enter fictitious offsetting trades [fact-11].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Reveal the January 2008 discovery: Kerviel had masked tens of billions of euros in unhedged directional bets, forcing a 3-day liquidation in a falling market that cost Société Générale €4.9 billion ($7.2 billion) [fact-11].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Hook Part 2: Quantifying Derivatives Leverage, Institutional Scale, and Rogue Losses

beatOutlines.textOutline: Display the €4.9 billion ($7.2 billion) Société Générale rogue trading loss alongside historical precedents: Nick Leeson's $1 billion loss at Barings Bank (1995) and John Rusnak's $700 million loss at Allied Irish Bank (2002) [fact-11].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Highlight the 10x profit amplification ($7,000 options net profit vs. $700 stock profit on a $2,000 outlay when a $20 stock hits $27) that lures speculators into leveraged derivatives [fact-08].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Anchor the institutional scale: over $2 trillion in global hedge fund assets under management operating under the '2-and-20' fee structure (2% management fee, 20% performance fee) [fact-10].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Options Core Architecture: Calls vs. Puts, Exercise Styles & Price Dynamics

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Call Options (right to buy at strike price) against Put Options (right to sell at strike price), emphasizing that holders pay an up-front option premium for choice without obligation [fact-01].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Contrast European options (exercisable only on the exact maturity date) against American options (exercisable at any time during the contract's life up to expiration) [fact-01].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Contrast strike and maturity pricing rules: as strike price increases, call prices decrease while put prices increase; as time to maturity increases, both call and put options become more valuable [fact-02].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: CBOE Google Options Case Study: Long Dec $550 Call vs. Short Sept $525 Put

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot the Long Google Dec $550 Call (1 contract = 100 shares, $29.00 offer, $2,900 up-front cost): show the flat -$2,900 capped loss when stock closes at or below $550 [fact-01, fact-03].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Trace the Long Call at $650 stock price: exercising buys 100 shares at $550 and sells at $650 for a $10,000 gross payoff, minus the $2,900 premium for a $7,100 net profit [fact-03].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot the Short Google Sept $525 Put ($22.40 bid, $2,240 immediate cash inflow): above $525 the option expires worthless and the writer keeps the $2,240 maximum profit; at $480 the writer faces a $4,500 gross assignment loss and a $2,260 net loss ($4,500 - $2,240) [fact-04].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: The Hedger's Dilemma: Fixing Prices with Forwards vs. Buying Insurance with Puts

beatOutlines.textOutline: Demonstrate corporate forward hedging (Example 1.1): ImportCo buys £10M 3-month forward at 1.5742 USD/GBP to lock in a $15,742,000 payment, while ExportCo sells £30M forward at 1.5736 USD/GBP to lock in $47,208,000 in proceeds [fact-05].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Highlight the forward trade-off: forward hedging neutralizes risk completely by fixing the price, eliminating downside loss but also surrendering any gain from favorable market moves [fact-05].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Contrast with option hedging (Example 1.2): an investor holding 1,000 shares at $28 ($28,000 value) buys 10 July $27.50 put contracts at $1 ($1,000 cost), guaranteeing a $27.50 liquidation price ($26,500 net floor) while preserving full upside participation [fact-06].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: The Speculator's Leverage: Spot vs. CME Futures & Shares vs. Call Options

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare £250,000 FX speculation (Table 1.4): buying spot GBP at 1.5470 requires $386,750 cash, whereas going long 4 CME April futures at 1.5410 requires only $20,000 initial margin [fact-07].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Race the FX outcomes: if GBP rises to 1.6000, futures yield $14,750 profit on $20,000 margin vs. $13,250 spot profit on $386,750; if GBP falls to 1.5000, futures lose $10,250 vs. an $11,750 spot loss [fact-07].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare $2,000 equity speculation (Table 1.5): buying 100 shares at $20 vs. buying 2,000 two-month $22.50 call options at $1; at $27 stock price, options earn $7,000 net profit vs. $700 share profit (10x higher), while at $15 stock price, options lose $2,000 (100%) vs. a $500 share loss [fact-08].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: The Arbitrageur's Blueprint: Cross-Border Dual-Listed Stock Arbitrage

beatOutlines.textOutline: Present the dual-listed market quotes (Example 1.3): a stock trades at $152 in New York and £100 in London while the spot exchange rate is $1.5500/£ [fact-09].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Step through the simultaneous execution and formula: buy 100 shares in New York for $15,200, sell 100 shares in London for £10,000, and convert £10,000 at $1.5500/£ into $15,500 to lock in 100 × [($1.55 × 100) - $152] = $300 riskless profit [fact-09].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Explain the self-correcting market equilibrium: arbitrage buying in New York pushes the USD price up while selling in London pushes the GBP price down until the discrepancy disappears [fact-09].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Inside the $2 Trillion Hedge Fund Ecosystem: '2-and-20' & Six Core Strategies

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 1 — Regulatory Structure & '2-and-20' Fees: Hedge funds manage over $2 trillion globally outside mutual fund rules on daily redemptions, leverage, and disclosures, charging a 2% annual management fee plus a 20% performance fee on profits [fact-10].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 2 — Relative-Value & Event Strategies: Long/Short Equities (long undervalued, short overvalued), Convertible Arbitrage (long convertible bonds, short equity), Distressed Securities (near-bankruptcy debt/equity), and Merger Arbitrage (post-takeover announcement spreads) [fact-10].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 3 — Macro & Developing Market Strategies: Emerging Markets (developing nation corporate/sovereign debt and equity) and Global Macro (high-conviction directional bets on macroeconomic trends) [fact-10].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 4 — Institutional Risk Control Failure: How Kerviel (SocGen, €4.9B loss in 2008), Leeson (Barings, $1B loss in 1995), and Rusnak (Allied Irish Bank, $700M loss in 2002) disguised unhedged directional bets inside arbitrage or FX mandates [fact-11].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Active Recall Challenge: Calculating Leveraged Option Payoffs vs. Stock Returns

beatOutlines.textOutline: Present the Table 1.5 setup: $2,000 capital deployed either into 100 shares at $20 or 2,000 two-month $22.50 strike call options at a $1 premium [fact-08].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Prompt the learner to compute the exact net profit at a $27 expiration price and the exact loss at a $15 expiration price, separating gross payoff from net profit after option premium [fact-01, fact-08].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Reveal the verified solution: at $27, options generate (2,000 × $4.50) - $2,000 = $7,000 net profit vs. $700 on shares (10x amplification); at $15, options lose the full $2,000 premium (100% loss) vs. $500 on shares [fact-08].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Practical Trader's Checklist: Matching Mandate, Instrument, and Risk Limit

beatOutlines.textOutline: Checklist Step 1 — Deduct Premium Before Sizing: Always subtract the up-front premium ($2,900 on the Google Dec $550 call) from gross exercise payoff, and remember that short puts ($2,240 inflow on Google Sept $525 put) carry heavy downside assignment risk ($2,260 net loss at $480) [fact-03, fact-04].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Checklist Step 2 — Choose Forward vs. Option Hedge Deliberately: Use forwards when locking in an exact budget (like ImportCo's $15,742,000 or ExportCo's $47,208,000) and protective puts when you need a downside floor ($26,500 net floor) while keeping upside gains [fact-05, fact-06].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Checklist Step 3 — Enforce Unambiguous Risk Limits: Whether trading leveraged futures ($20,000 margin controlling £250,000), 20-contract option positions, or institutional arbitrage desks, monitor positions daily so unauthorized directional bets cannot masquerade as hedged trades [fact-07, fact-08, fact-11].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Chapter Synthesis: 8 Core Rules of Options, Traders, and Risk Management

beatOutlines.textOutline: Synthesize options definitions, European vs. American exercise rules, strike/maturity price dynamics, and the 100-share Google call and put calculations [fact-01, fact-02, fact-03, fact-04].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Synthesize the three trader archetypes across forward vs. put hedging, futures vs. options speculation, and cross-border dual-listed arbitrage [fact-05, fact-06, fact-07, fact-08, fact-09].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Synthesize hedge fund '2-and-20' mechanics, the six institutional strategies, and the compliance lessons from Kerviel (€4.9B), Leeson ($1B), and Rusnak ($700M) [fact-10, fact-11].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: 1. Right Without Obligation: Calls grant the right to buy and puts grant the right to sell at a strike price by expiration for an up-front premium; European options exercise only at maturity while American options exercise at any time [fact-01].
2. Strike & Maturity Pricing Rules: Higher strike prices reduce call values and increase put values, while longer time to maturity increases the value of both calls and puts [fact-02].

3. Long Call vs. Short Put Mechanics: Buying 1 Google Dec $550 call for $2,900 caps loss at $2,900 and nets $7,100 profit at $650 [fact-03]; writing 1 Google Sept $525 put for $2,240 caps profit at $2,240 and incurs a $2,260 net loss at $480 [fact-04].

4. Forward Hedging vs. Option Insurance: Currency forwards fix exact payments ($15,742,000 for ImportCo; $47,208,000 for ExportCo) by removing both downside and upside [fact-05], whereas buying 10 July $27.50 puts for $1,000 on 1,000 shares at $28 guarantees a $26,500 net floor while keeping upside gains [fact-06].

5. Speculating with Futures Leverage: Controlling £250,000 via 4 CME April futures at 1.5410 requires $20,000 margin vs. $386,750 spot cash at 1.5470, yielding +$14,750 at 1.6000 or -$10,250 at 1.5000 [fact-07].

6. Speculating with Options Leverage: Deploying $2,000 into 2,000 calls ($22.50 strike at $1) instead of 100 shares at $20 magnifies profit 10x at $27 ($7,000 vs. $700) but risks a 100% loss ($2,000 vs. $500) at $15 [fact-08].

7. Cross-Border Riskless Arbitrage: Buying 100 shares in NY at $152 ($15,200) and simultaneously selling in London at £100 ($15,500 at $1.5500/£) locks in a $300 risk-free profit while driving prices toward equilibrium [fact-09].

8. Hedge Funds & Rogue Risk Controls: Over $2 trillion in hedge fund AUM operates under '2-and-20' fees across six core strategies [fact-10], while rogue losses by Kerviel (€4.9B), Leeson ($1B), and Rusnak ($700M) prove that daily verification of offsetting hedges is mandatory [fact-11].
bottomTakeaway: Options and futures empower traders to hedge risk, amplify speculative views, or capture riskless arbitrage, but survival in derivatives markets requires accounting for up-front premiums and enforcing strict daily risk controls [fact-01, fact-05, fact-08, fact-09, fact-11].
